mechanisms.decisive_claim: Distinct nontrivial bipartitions of r private primes encode every incidence at every host vertex with fixed shared point product.
mechanisms.kill_test: Verify the bipartition count and global prime budget for arbitrary maximum degree.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Two private primes with complementary exponent pairs encode all incident edges within the same asymptotic bit budget.
mechanisms.kill_test: Prove the minimum exponent range for Delta distinct pairs and compare its bit cost with logarithmic block coding.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Prime blocks may be reused at nonadjacent host vertices without compromising global injectivity.
mechanisms.kill_test: Test two reused blocks that occur in private vertices on different host edges.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every constructed alternating equal-product relation is a primitive circuit of its complete prime-valuation matrix.
mechanisms.kill_test: Solve the rational kernel using one private prime row per path edge and verify the primitive integral generator.
mechanisms.status_evidence: evidence/FAITHFUL_LINEAR_EMBEDDING.md Section 3 and finite path-prime propagation replay

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The published toric hypergraph encoding theorem directly supplies the required bounded-band arithmetic labeling and cover-number preservation.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compare the stated outputs of the toric encoding theorem with the frozen arithmetic, scale, and transversal requirements.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Linearity alone makes the prime-block footprints preserve every pairwise edge intersection exactly, while private vertices remain edge-unique.
mechanisms.kill_test: Check all shared-shared, shared-private, endpoint-endpoint, endpoint-internal, and internal-internal collision cases.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Classical graph set-intersection representations alone preserve the host hypergraph transversal number after arithmetic conversion.
mechanisms.kill_test: Test whether graph adjacency data determines shared host vertices and hypergraph transversals.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Replacing every edge-private arithmetic vertex by a shared host vertex from the same edge proves exact equality of transversal numbers.
mechanisms.kill_test: Prove both inequalities and test replacements when several private choices map to the same host vertex.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: For every edge size m>K, an explicit quotient-remainder decrement vector has sum Delta, maximum four, and balances the two-adic exponents exactly.
mechanisms.kill_test: Derive the ceiling-discrepancy interval and display the exponent-sum identity after decrements.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Several padding primes remove the minimum edge size m>K without strengthening the raw-value budget.
mechanisms.kill_test: Test capacity for m<=K and determine whether all padding exponents remain nonnegative in a fixed band.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The same two-block footprint construction preserves exact intersections for arbitrary non-linear host hypergraphs without modification.
mechanisms.kill_test: Place one vertex pair in two distinct host edges and compare their internal private footprints.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Preserving only the edge-intersection graph is sufficient to preserve the host transversal number.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compare hypergraphs with the same edge-intersection graph but different shared-vertex multiplicities and cover numbers.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Cloning vertices inside every short edge until its size exceeds K preserves simplicity, linearity, matching number, and transversal number and therefore removes the minimum-edge-size hypothesis.
mechanisms.kill_test: Check whether cloned vertices create extra shared intersections or change minimum covers.
